summary: Make replicated last-activity timestamps independent of delivery order

replay.detail: The individual and batched roster readers select the greatest numeric acceptance time directly from their snapshot's claims; no replay is required.

schema.detail: Five local partial indexes support acceptance-time seeks for work, sent/received messages, legacy timeline activity and the harness fold. The obsolete actor-progress arrival index is removed. A one-million-row synthetic store measured 59,101,184 additional live index bytes and 13,058,048 bytes reclaimed by dropping the old index (46,043,136 net live bytes); freed pages can be reused. The schema version and replicated projection layout are unchanged.

rules.detail: No checkpoint, retention, authority or admission rule change.

compatibility.detail: Response fields and wire format are unchanged. Receiving an older replicated activity claim no longer moves the last-activity timestamp backward.

downtime.detail: The first normal open builds the indexes synchronously in open-store before API listeners bind. On a warm synthetic SQLite 3.46.0 store with 1,000,000 initial mixed claims (2,503,114,752 live bytes), the five builds plus final WAL checkpoint took 17.080 seconds and the obsolete index drop took 0.071 seconds. This measures index work, not total daemon startup or a cold/live-store forecast. Allow this startup phase to finish; startup readiness reports it.

manual.detail: No configuration or manual SQL. The first restart includes the measured synchronous index installation before serving.

recovery.detail: The corrected readers derive activity from the existing claim log; SQLite installs each local index atomically. There is no replay or claim deletion.
